head: efab6732de4f15327bc356a720f88d4d8d0adf41
summary:
Attempt 2 (efab673) replaces the parent comparison in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:177-185 with the accepted leaf-based rewrite. It captures only mkdtemp's ASCII leaf with '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at .*[\\/](fsa-rules-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*$'. It then removes [IO.Path]::Combine(folder, leaf) for each of GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP where that folder exists. The mkdtemp charset (a-z, 0-9, _) is covered. The greedy `.*[\\/]` takes the last separator, so a `\xe9` escape earlier in the path cannot split the leaf. `\s*$` absorbs CR.

What I ran:
- **Default suite:** tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 held every check under pwsh 7.6 (Space, TempNotTmp, ShortName, NonAscii, Refused), exit 0. It also held under Windows PowerShell 5.1, exit 0. SL-069 runs RuleCases.ps1 under 5.1, and both files are pure ASCII.
- **Python shape:** -Shape Python with the real harness.py held for the space/TEMP≠TMP, 8.3 and non-ASCII spellings. No fsa-rules-* was left.
- **Bite check:** I ran the same test against a copy of attempt-1's RuleCases.ps1 (git show f80d776). It failed exactly ShortName, NonAscii and the new Refused 'fsa-rules-sl076 copy' case, 3 checks. So the new shapes feed the shapes they name.

Safety: a folder is removed only if its name is exactly mkdtemp's and it sits directly in TMP or TEMP. A TMPDIR scratch is left alone, not mis-deleted, because the random leaf will not exist in TMP/TEMP.

One new defect: the Shape-Refused comment still describes the attempt-1 mechanism and is now false.

Second round: This round found nothing new in the attempt-2 code. m3 from this attempt's first round, the stale Shape-Refused comment, still stands.

**The new pattern**, tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:177, run on hand-made inputs:
- It takes the leaf correctly from:
  - a CRLF line inside a multi-line block, with a space and a '\xe9' escape in the path;
  - a trailing tab;
  - no final newline;
  - forward slashes.
- It refuses:
  - an indented line, so a nested say() line cannot match;
  - a leaf with a suffix, such as 'fsa-rules-abc.old';
  - RuleCases' own 'fsa-rules-case-*' names. Its hyphen is outside the character class, so those folders can never be targeted.
- A lone CR does not match. That cannot reach the pattern: Python on Windows prints CRLF, and PowerShell splits native output on any line break, and Out-String rejoins it with CRLF.

**One match per run:** harness.py prints exactly one kept line at column 0 (:734). Every other say() line is indented or is a traceback, so reading only the first match is correct. No RuleCases case passes --keep or reads the scratch after Invoke-HarnessRaw returns.

**Boundaries:**
- A null $env:TEMP is filtered out.
- TMP equal to TEMP, or a TMP that does not exist, only means one extra Test-Path that returns false.
- A TMPDIR scratch cannot be mis-deleted: its random leaf does not exist in TMP or TEMP.

**Partial failure:** Remove-Item with SilentlyContinue can leave part of a folder behind. That predates this slice, and the builder's real C-006 and C-014 runs measured nothing left.

**Shells:** the test holds under both pwsh 7.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1, and both files are pure ASCII.

findings.claim: The comment heading Shape-Refused still describes the attempt-1 mechanism and is now false twice over. (1) Invoke-HarnessRaw no longer reads the line whole, and no guard decides on a read path. For 'not-rules' and the new 'fsa-rules-sl076 copy' it is the leaf pattern that refuses them by not matching. For 'elsewhere' and 'deeper' the printed path is never used; the leaf is only looked up in TMP/TEMP. (2) 'No space' is contradicted by the case this attempt added right below it, 'fsa-rules-sl076 copy'. A reader told that 'only the guard decides' will not see that these cases now prove the pattern refuses non-mkdtemp names and that the printed parent is ignored. They could loosen the pattern (e.g. to 'fsa-rules-\S+') thinking a separate guard backs it.
findings.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1:176 `# No space in this TEMP, so each line is read whole by either pattern and only the guard decides.`, above :181 `(Join-Path $temp 'fsa-rules-sl076 copy')`. tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:177-185 now reads only the leaf.
findings.fix: Reword the comment to: '# Nothing here is a folder mkdtemp made directly in TMP or TEMP: the pattern takes only an fsa-rules-[A-Za-z0-9_]+ leaf, and that leaf is looked for only directly in TMP and TEMP, never at the printed path.'

obligations.evidence: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:177-185 no longer compares a printed parent. The leaf is joined to GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP, so an 8.3 TEMP is found through either (GetTempPath expands it, and $env:TEMP is used raw). Shape-ShortName (tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1:158-165) sets TMP=TEMP to an FSO ShortPath ('...\FSEC9F~1\Users\JOHNSM~1\...'). It passed here and failed against attempt-1's RuleCases. The Python shape's 8.3 spelling with the real harness.py also passed.

tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:177 captures only the ASCII leaf, so say()'s '\xe9' escape (harness.py:72) no longer matters. Shape-NonAscii (tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1:167-172) sets TMP=TEMP under 'José Smith', and its stand-in prints through Get-Said, the say() escaping. It passed here under pwsh 7 and 5.1 and failed against attempt-1's RuleCases. The Python shape's non-ASCII spelling left no fsa-rules-*.
The Space and TempNotTmp shapes still pass on the rewritten Invoke-HarnessRaw, and the Python shape's space/TEMP≠TMP spelling left nothing in TMP or TEMP.

cases.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 takes RuleCases' own Invoke-HarnessRaw from its AST. It feeds a spaced TEMP (Space), TEMP≠TMP (TempNotTmp, which also asserts GetTempPath returned TMP), an 8.3 TEMP (ShortName) and a non-ASCII TEMP printed escaped (NonAscii). It asserts removal by Test-Path -LiteralPath. Refused covers four folders that must be left alone. The Python shape runs the real harness.py for three spellings. Against attempt-1 code the new shapes fail, so they bite.

drift: The design's key decision still reads 'Accept the folder when its leaf is fsa-rules-* and its parent is either GetTempPath or $env:TEMP'. The code now ignores the printed parent entirely and looks the mkdtemp leaf up directly in GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP. This departure is declared: it is the rewrite accepted in the m1/m2 decisions. A reader checking against the design document alone will find it out of date.

Declared, not built: the send-back's suggestion to delete an exact recorded scratch path. RuleCases never makes the harness's scratch, so it has no path to record other than the printed line. The reasoning holds against the code.
No new drift. The leaf lookup in GetTempPath()/$env:TEMP replaces the design's parent comparison. That was declared through the accepted m1/m2 decisions, as recorded last round.
